newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Piltel down four pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Piltel down four pct in late trade.

text.p: Cellular phone firm Pilipino Telephone Corp shed 75 centavos, or four percent, to 18.75 pesos in late trade on Tuesday on news its 1996 net income will be lower than expected at about 700 million pesos, brokers said.

"The weakness of the stock came about because of its announcement that its net income will be about 700 million pesos for 1996 when most of us have predicted over a billion pesos," said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securities.
A recent Reuters poll of seven brokerage houses showed the company was expected to post a 19 percent rise in net income for 1996 to 978.76 million pesos.
In a statement on Monday, the company said it sees its net income last year "in the vicinity" of 700 million pesos, despite a provision of 887 million pesos for doubtful accounts.
The provision includes a one-time recognition of 740 million pesos in bad debts for 1996 due to subscriber fraud and delinquency as well as contested bills due to cloning.

"Sentiment on Piltel is expected to remain weak until investors will see a clear indication of improvement in its cloning and receivable situation," another broker from a foreign brokerage house said.
In late trade on Tuesday, Piltel was the fifth most actively traded issue with value turnover at 109.742 million pesos.
